subject: Finity pilot - p50/p95 measurement windows and emergency fallback proposal
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@finity.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: p50/p95 commitments for the pilot (measurement window)

Hi Rafael / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo — Finity's engineering team is reviewing performance and we have two operational questions before we sign the pilot MSA:

1) How do you define the p50 and p95 commitments for the hosted API? Specifically, what measurement window do you use (rolling 24h, calendar day, sample-based)?
2) We have predictable month-end batch spikes (10x baseline for ~3 hours). Are bursts carved out or treated as normal traffic for SLOs?

We're sensitive to commitments for the pilot because we'll rely on them in our runbook (fallback to cached responses or smaller model). Can you share your proposal and any exception process?

Thanks — Alex
Sam Park will join procurement on our side (procurement@finity.ai).

--
Alex Wu
Head of Platform, Finity.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@finity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: p50/p95 commitments for the pilot (measurement window)

Alex — great questions, and very timely. Attached is a short draft (latency_slo_draft_v2.pdf) that spells out how we measure p50/p95 and our exception paths for predictable spikes. High level:

- Measurement baseline: rolling 30-day window aggregated with a two-tier sampling approach (1-minute buckets for p50, 5-minute buckets for p95) to capture both steady-state and short-term burst behavior. We avoid strict calendar-day boundaries for fairness across timezones.
- Commitments: for the pilot we can commit to p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 850ms from edge ingress to token-ready response for our hosted eu/us regions, measured using the above window and bucket strategy.
- Burst treatment: we offer a "predictable-burst carveout" where customers can nominate recurring batch windows; those windows are excluded from p95 calculation if the burst is provably traffic-driven (we require a 7-day historical pattern and pre-notification + sampling evidence).
- Emergency fallback: automatic model variant downgrade (same model family, smaller context/quantized) + best-effort cached prefix responses to keep tail latency bounded during sustained overloads; we'll route to a lower-cost capacity tier in fallback so availability remains intact.

A few questions for you that will determine whether Finity qualifies for the predictable-burst carveout:
- Can you share the monthly traffic sample (CSV) you mentioned and confirm the typical month-end timeline?
- Do you need legal-grade SLA language in the pilot MSA or is an operational playbook sufficient for now?

I'll loop in Product / SRE (Ben / Priyom) for specifics on the measurement implementation and evidence requirements.

Next steps: we can turn the attached draft into an addendum to the pilot MSA if you want formalized terms.

Cheers,
Rafael
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: p50/p95 commitments for the pilot (measurement window)

Rafael — internal notes and proposed tweaks before we send the formal addendum to Finity:

On sampling and buckets:
- We should be explicit that 1-minute buckets are sampled at ingress with per-request trace ids so we can reconstitute tail events; that supports audit requirements.
- For p95 we should use sliding 30-day with a 3-hour rolling warmup window so short maintenance windows don't skew the metric.

On carveouts:
- Approve the predictable-burst carveout but require:
  * 7-day pre-notification for the first pilot month, then 48h for established repeats
  * Finity must provide the CSV evidence (attachment they referenced) and an ID for the recurring job triggering the spike
- If they cannot meet evidence requirements, offer a temporary regional routing policy (route Finity to a dedicated pool during peak hours) as a paid addon.

On commitments:
- For pilot commercials we can soften p95 in writing to <= 1.0s with a remediation SLA (credits if monthly p95 > 1.5s for two consecutive months) — that buys time while we optimize their traffic patterns.

I'll draft a short addendum template and attach it to the HubSpot deal (see link). If Marissa signs off we can send to Alex + procurement.

-Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@finity.ai>, Sam Park <sam.park@finity.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: p50/p95 commitments for the pilot (measurement window)

Alex / Sam — thanks for raising this. We reviewed the proposal and are comfortable with the operational approach Rafael shared and Ben's tweaks. To summarize what Redwood will commit to for the Finity pilot: 

1) Measurement: sliding 30-day window with 1-minute buckets for p50 and 5-minute buckets for p95; a 3-hour rolling warmup to avoid maintenance noise.
2) Pilot commitments: p50 <= 120ms (ingress -> token-ready) and p95 <= 1.0s (ingress -> token-ready) for the US region.
3) Predictable-burst carveout: eligible if Finity supplies 7 days of historical traffic evidence and provides 7-day advance notice for month-end spikes during the first month (48h thereafter). If evidence is not available, Redwood will offer dedicated regional routing during nominated windows as an alternative (paid).
4) Remediation: if monthly p95 > 1.5s for two consecutive months we will issue a service credit equal to 10% of that month’s hosted usage for Finity.

Please review and confirm whether you prefer an addendum to the pilot MSA or an operational playbook attachment. Rafael will draft the addendum and share the HubSpot link (and DocuSign) after we hear from you.

Looking forward to getting Finity into pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
